c6_iris.place: Bellwether, the market and the pier

chapter.title: Iris
chapter.goal: Steve wants to free Calder and learn what the Veyri want.

c6_iris.coach: Two investigators now. Each lead shows who should handle it. Press Q or use the name menu at the top right to switch.
c6_iris.objective: Meet the stranger who warned you about Rook. Keep the town looking somewhere else.
notes: Iris’s turn at the waterline on the 30th (Chapter 3 stakeout) was her second missed re-sync, on purpose. The first, on the 21st, was an accident. She says so in the takes lead.
New sound assets for hold: effect.halcyon_hold_seattle and effect.halcyon_hold_denver. Different clerks, different ring counts, the same eight bars of hold music ending on the same note.
The text message line uses display_text to show the message as typed.
Iris is shown as “Nora’s copy” until out.03, where she names herself. From c6_jail on she is “Iris”.
context: steve|Stephen and I spent the weekend in Dad’s shack, arguing about haircuts. He won every argument.
steve|On Monday morning my flip phone buzzed.

intro.new: autorick|Police are seeking Steve Mercer, last seen wearing a cardigan. Yesterday he was sunny.
steve|“Pier. Eight-ten. Come alone. Please.” No capitals. Same as the warning about Rook.
intro.display_text: “pier. 8:10. come alone. please.” No capitals. Same as the warning about Rook.

alibi.title: Market corner
alibi.goal: Give the town a sighting of Steve’s face across town at exactly 8:10.
alibi.background: At 8:10 Steve meets the texter on the pier. If someone in town sees Steve’s face somewhere else at that same minute, the search goes there instead. Stephen has three errands, and each one runs on a different clock.
lead: stephen|Three errands, three clocks. Nobody in this town agrees what time it is.
stephen|Gus sets his oven clock four minutes fast. He says it keeps the bread honest.
stephen|The bus clock runs two minutes slow. The florist sets hers by the radio, like a sensible person.
stephen|And Gus has my poster in his window. He asks everyone to help him fix the smudge.
alibi.prompt: Which errand puts Stephen’s face in front of a witness at exactly 8:10 by the radio?

board.instruction: Put each slip on radio time, then pick the witness who will really see Stephen’s face.
evidence: Gus’s oven clock runs four minutes fast.
The bus clock runs two minutes slow, and the florist’s clock matches the radio.
The slips read BREAD 08:14, BUS 08:05 and FLOWERS 08:12.
The bus driver stamps fares without looking up, and the florist takes orders by phone.
Gus has a smudged wanted poster in his window, and he asks customers to help him fix it.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each question.
slots: Who will look at Stephen’s face?

board.wrong_text: Stephen checks his watch against the radio. Something doesn’t add up yet.

hints: Use the radio as the one true clock.
Take four minutes off Gus’s slip, and add two minutes to the bus slip.
Only one slip lands on 08:10, and only one witness looks a customer in the face.

lines.text: Good morning. Yes, that’s my face on the poster. Terrible photograph.

alibi.finding: steve|At 8:10 by the radio, Stephen stood beside his own wanted poster at Gus’s bread window while Gus fixed the smudge. Half the town is searching the market.

takes.title: Iris’s recorder test
takes.goal: Test her fairly, the way you tested Nora’s good morning.
takes.background: On Sunday the 21st, Nora’s good morning came out the same, breath for breath, twice. Rook’s “Sit tight, June” did too. A recording always repeats. A person never quite does.

lead.text: I sent the message about Rook. No capitals, the way Nora texts. Please listen before you decide what I am.

lead: steve|You let me go on the balcony. And on the thirtieth you stopped at the waterline and walked home. I saw you.
iris|The first time I missed going below, it was an accident. I was chasing you. The second time, I chose.
steve|Then say something for me. Twice. “I stayed because I wanted to.”

lead.direction: second take; she pauses in a new place

takes.prompt: Steve gives her the recorder and asks for the same words twice. What can he put in his notebook?
options: She played the first take again
She chose how to say it each time
She started the same take later

wrong.0: Listen to the pause. The second take waits where the first one didn’t.
wrong.2: Line them up and they still don’t match. The rhythm inside the phrase changes.

hints: Listen past the words. Compare where each take goes quiet.
Starting one recording later wouldn’t change the spacing inside the phrase.
A replayed take keeps every pause in place, even if it starts later. Hers moved.
lines: c6_iris.takes.03
iris|Before I was Nora, I was a junior crew member with a duty and a record. We call ourselves Veyri. None of us had ever had a self.
takes.finding: steve|Two takes, two different rhythms. Copies replay. She chose her words each time. The tell has turned around.

hold.title: Halcyon lines
hold.goal: Find out how copies far from the bay stay in step.
hold.background: Copies near the bay walk into the water on the ninth night. Rook was hundreds of miles away, and he was always on hold with ‘the Bureau’. On the thirtieth, after she turned back from the water, Iris phoned two different Halcyon offices at four minutes past midnight and taped both calls.
lead: iris|You saw the ones near the bay go below. The ones far away call.
iris|At four minutes past midnight on the thirtieth, I phoned two Halcyon offices. I taped both calls.
hold.prompt: Neither call reached a person. Line up the two tapes. Which part matches exactly?
options: Eight bars of hold music, ending on the same note

wrong.0: Two different clerks, two different greetings.
wrong.1: One phone rings three times, the other five.

hints: Different offices, different clerks. What could they still share?
Skip the greetings and line up the music.
The greetings and the rings differ from office to office. Look for the part neither clerk controls.
lines: c6_iris.hold.01
c6_iris.hold.02
steve|Four minutes past midnight. That’s when the water lit up.
iris|Saren believes your mother wrote down how the engine works. A records officer told him so. I have never seen him want anything more.
iris|And on Wednesday, at the signing, he means to put a copy of your President in her chair. Her own physician scanned her weeks ago.
hold.finding: steve|Both calls share the same eight bars of hold music, at the minute the water lit up. Copies near the bay go below; copies far away wait on hold. Saren wants Mom’s notebook, and on Wednesday he wants the President.

recap: steve|Nora’s copy sent the warning about Rook. She stopped going into the water, and she doesn’t replay any more. She chooses.
steve|Copies far from the bay stay in step on hold. Saren wants Mom’s notebook, and on Wednesday he wants the President.
steve|And she told me about June. They scanned her at the safe house. Her copy took the Sheriff’s desk this morning, and the real June is in her own cell until the ninth night.

outro.text: Iris. After the flowers on the balcony.

lines: steve|Have you seen Admiral since you went missing?
iris|Once, at dawn on Saturday, when the pier was empty. He still won’t come to my whistle.
iris|He stole my sandwich anyway. I think that means we’re friends now.
steve|Do you even like breakfast? You always said you’d eaten already.
iris|I don’t like it. Nora doesn’t either. It was on a list of healthy things.
iris|This morning I skipped it. It felt like breaking a very small law.
iris|I miss Sunday dinners. Carmen shouting at the stove. Tomás explaining the moon landing to the soup.
steve|They miss you too. They think you’re Nora.
iris|I know. That is the part I can’t fix.
steve|Do you still think I need a haircut?
stephen|We both need one. I just look better needing it.
stephen|I slept in Dad’s chair last night. It still smells of solder and peppermints.
steve|He kept the peppermints in the drawer with the fuses.
stephen|Third drawer down. I know. I remember that part.
stephen|Everyone at the market is going to stare at me today.
steve|That’s the whole idea, Stephen.
stephen|I’ve never been the interesting one before. I could get used to it.

lines.new: autorick|Police are still looking for Steve Mercer. If you see him, tell him to smile!

lines: stephen|He never smiles before ten. I can vouch for that personally.

c6_jail.objective: Find the cell key, then work out which June is the real one.
notes: Both Junes use the calder voice. Line-level display tells them apart: “June at the desk” and “June in cell two”.
Pell names himself in the intro, so the display rule switches from “Dale Kittredge” to “Pell” in this scene.
distract and exit become rows puzzles (drop the case boards). The crossword test pays off Chapter 3: a fresh private fact, checked on paper.
Art (optional): Gus’s bakery van with a giant croissant on its roof, at the loading door, for the departure.
context: steve|The Sheriff’s office, at noon. June’s copy was at June’s desk, hunting me. June was in cell two.
intro: stephen|The Sheriff is at her desk. The Sheriff is also in cell two. One of those is a staffing problem.
pell|My name is Pell. Dale is asleep on the ship. I have worn his face for a year.
pell|I have fed Biscuit twice a day since the Sheriff went away. If I report you properly, they will reset me, and I will not remember her.

mail.title: Pell’s sorting case
mail.goal: Find the cell key in Pell’s sorting case.
mail.background: Pell files everything exactly by the rules. His sorting case has three drawers, labelled Counter, Returns and Jail. The jail’s cell key went back through the post this morning.
lead: pell|The cell key was returned to the post this morning. I filed it.
steve|Where?
pell|Correctly.
pell|I file by destination. The carbon says Jail, returned key. That is register entry eighteen.
pell|Each slot holds two entries. Slot one holds entries one and two, and so on.
mail.instruction: Find the drawer for where the key is going, then the slot that holds entry 18. Each slot holds two entries: slot 1 holds 1 and 2, slot 2 holds 3 and 4, and so on.
hints: Pell files by where a thing is going, not by what happened to it.
The returned key is entry 18. Two entries share each slot.
Slot 1 holds 1 and 2, slot 2 holds 3 and 4. Keep counting in pairs until you reach 18.
lines: c6_jail.mail.01

lines.new: steve|June’s own crossword is in the jail pile. I’ll circle one square and post it through her slot.

lines: steve|Twenty-three across, where it crosses eight down. Only the real June will know that square.
mail.finding: steve|The key was in the Jail drawer, slot 9, where entries 17 and 18 share a slot. And on today’s crossword I circled the square where 23 Across crosses 8 Down, and posted it through June’s slot. Only she has it.

distract.title: Sheriff’s front desk
distract.goal: Keep the records deputy away from the cell corridor long enough for Steve to reach June.
distract.background: When a wanted poster is contested, the records deputy has to fetch the original file from the basement, and the man in question has to stand at the likeness counter while the clerk compares his face with the poster.
lead: stephen|Three tickets at the counter. Leave the deputy to me.
stephen|The clerk says a contested likeness sends the deputy down to the basement for the file.
steve|She leaves at 11:59 and she’s back at 12:03. I need two clear minutes.
distract.prompt: Which ticket should Stephen take, and when should Steve go in and come out?
distract.instruction: Pick the ticket that keeps Stephen’s face at the counter, then fit Steve’s two minutes inside the time the deputy is away. Ticket 41: pay a fine at the cashier. Ticket 42: contest a likeness, in person, at the counter. Ticket 43: drop a form through the slot. The deputy leaves at 11:59 and is back at 12:03.
hints: Which ticket needs Stephen’s face, in person, for the whole appointment?
The deputy leaves at 11:59 and is back at 12:03. Steve’s two minutes have to fit strictly inside that.
Only one ticket needs Stephen’s face at the counter for the whole appointment. Steve’s two minutes must start after 11:59 and end before 12:03.
lines: c6_jail.distract.01
distract.finding: steve|Stephen contested his own wanted poster at the likeness counter. The deputy went down to the basement at 11:59. I was in the corridor from 12:00 to 12:02, and out before she came back.

crossword.title: The two Junes
crossword.goal: Find out which June is the real one.
crossword.background: Last week June told Steve that memories can’t prove who she is: “You check my paperwork, same as everyone else.” A copy made at the safe house would remember everything up to Thursday, and nothing that happened in that cell.

lead.new: calder|Mercer. That woman in cell two is a copy. Don’t you dare let her out.
calder|He’ll check my paperwork, Mercer. I taught him that.

lead: steve|I’ll ask them both which letter I circled this morning. Only one of them has seen it.
crossword.prompt: Each June answers on a slip of paper. What should Steve ask, and which answer should he accept?
crossword.instruction: Ask about the square Steve circled, then accept the slip with the right letter. 23 Across, ‘beyond imitation’, is INIMITABLE, shown as I _ I _ I _ A _ L _. Its first, second and last blanks cross 3 Down, 8 Down and 12 Down.
hints: Steve said which square he circled when he found the key. His notebook has it too.
Write INIMITABLE under the blanks, one letter at a time.
Find the blank that crosses the down clue Steve chose, and read the letter there.
lines: steve|Desk June circled a T. Close. Wrong.
c6_jail.crossword.02
crossword.finding: steve|Only the June in cell two knew which square I circled: the M where 23 Across crosses 8 Down. The June at the desk guessed a T. We have the real one.

exit.title: Deputy’s checkpoint
exit.goal: Get past Lyle’s copy at the checkpoint without a fight.
exit.background: Lyle’s copy is on duty at the back checkpoint. His relief signed in at 18:24. Tonight his son Ben is in the school play, and the school doors close at 18:40.
lead: lyle_copy|Sheriff. Steve. I’m supposed to stop you.
lyle_copy|Ben’s a tree in the school play tonight. He’s been practising being a tree for a month.
calder|Lyle. Your relief has signed.
calder|The school doors close at six forty. Let’s find you the fastest way there.
exit.prompt: Can Lyle still make it? Tell him the fastest way.
exit.instruction: Lyle can leave the moment his relief signs, at 18:24. Walking to the school takes 18 minutes. Bus A leaves at 18:29 and takes 9 minutes. Bus B leaves at 18:26 and takes 15 minutes. The school doors close at 18:40.
hints: Add each trip to the time Lyle can start it.
Walking: 18:24 plus 18 minutes. Bus A: 18:29 plus 9. Bus B: 18:26 plus 15.
Walking gets Lyle there at 18:42, two minutes late. Work out both buses the same way.

lines.text: Bus A. Twenty-nine past. They gave me a seat in the front row.

lines: c6_jail.exit.02
exit.finding: steve|Lyle’s copy could still make Ben’s play: Bus A at 18:29, at the school by 18:38. He chose the front row over his orders, and let us go.

recap: steve|June is out of her cell, and her copy is still at her desk, hunting me. Pell chose a beagle over his orders. Lyle’s copy chose a school play.
steve|Five fugitives and a beagle. We needed a car nobody would look for.

outro.direction: at the bakery loading door, holding out the keys to a van with a giant croissant on its roof

outro: steve|Iris. The ring in my sock drawer. Did Nora ever find it?
iris|A copy who stops going below starts to forget. Nora’s memories go first.

lines: steve|How is Biscuit doing these days?
pell|She eats at seven and at five. She prefers the blue bowl. I am not yet sure she prefers me.
pell|I am working on it. I have learned to scratch behind her left ear.
steve|Do you like the mail route?
pell|Dale’s route has two hundred and twelve stops. Dale liked eleven of them.
pell|I have started to like a twelfth. Carmen gives me a churro at La Marea. The real Dale never stopped there.
steve|What is Dale like? The real one.
pell|He complains about the rain, the dogs and the government. In that order.
pell|I have his memories, but not his complaints. I find I do not miss them.
iris|Who is feeding the otters while I’m away from the aquarium?
steve|The volunteers. Including the one who got bitten.
iris|Good. She’s brave. The pups like brave people.
stephen|The clerk said I looked nothing like my poster.
steve|It is my poster. It is literally my face.
stephen|I told her that. She said I was far too cheerful to be you.
calder|I spent the morning in my own cell. That mattress is worse than I ever admitted.
steve|You told the county the cells were fine.
calder|I told the county a lot of things. I’m ordering new mattresses.
calder|Pell has been feeding my dog? Twice a day?
steve|Blue bowl, seven and five. He’s learned the left ear.
calder|Then he can keep his job. Don’t you dare tell him I said that.
calder|She does my paperwork better than I do. That’s what bothers me most.
steve|She guessed a T, June. She didn’t know you.
calder|No. She knew my files. That isn’t the same thing at all.

i2_nora.when: Monday night, inside the Long Patience
i2_nora.coach: You are Nora, awake on the ship. The guard walks a regular lap. Count it before you move.
i2_nora.objective: Wake the others, learn their names and find a way through the Gallery.
notes: Nora wakes because Iris stopped re-syncing. Nora doesn’t know that; the player does.
jobs keeps the case board with a single stage (the route and logging stages are cut).
The eye under the frost is narrated in the departure. Art (optional): an insert of Row Zero with one enormous eye open under cracked frost.
Nora plays this interlude, so her small talk is with Dale and Lyle, the two sleepers awake beside her.
context: nora|I woke up in amber light, in a bed I didn’t choose, in a hall that went on forever.
nora|I was frightened for about a minute. Then I did what I do at any party where nobody knows each other. I started learning names.

patrol.title: Guard circuit
patrol.goal: Find a safe moment to cross the aisle.
patrol.background: A guard walks the Gallery in laps. Nora counts under her breath and scratches marks on her bed rail.
lead: nora|Boots. Then the pump. Then the far door. Again and again.
nora|Once that far door shuts, he can’t see the aisle. Crossing takes me four counts.
patrol.prompt: When should Nora step out, and when will she reach cover?
patrol.instruction: Step out when the far door shuts, and reach cover before the boots come back. Lap one: boots at 2, pump at 5, far door shuts at 8. The boots come back at 14, and the lap repeats. Crossing takes four counts.
hints: Find the length of one whole lap from the boots.
The door shuts six counts after the boots. Add four counts for the crossing.
The lap is twelve counts long. Find the next time the door shuts after 14, then add four.
lines: i2_nora.patrol.01
patrol.finding: nora|The guard’s lap is twelve counts. On the next lap the far door shuts at 20 and the boots come back at 26. Four counts to cross. We can move.

jobs.title: Sleeper skills
jobs.goal: Give each half-awake sleeper the job they’re already good at.
jobs.background: Three sleepers are awake enough to help: Nora, the real Lyle Boone and a grumpy mail carrier named Dale. Nora has watched each of them for hours.
lead: nora|Everybody’s good at something. Even Dale.
lyle|That hatch sticks. I’ve wedged it open twice already tonight.
dale|Thirty years on a mail route. I could walk this one with my eyes shut.
jobs.prompt: Who keeps the hatch, who guides at the fork, and who reads the gauges?

board.instruction: Give each person the job they have already practised.
evidence: Lyle has wedged the sticking hatch open twice.
Dale can recite every turn of the route with his eyes shut.
Nora has drawn the whole water circuit in pencil, gauges and all.
The route runs through the sticking hatch, then a fork with no arrows, then the gauge cabinets.

stages.prompt: Put one name on each job.
slots: Who keeps the sticking hatch open?
Who guides everyone at the fork?

board.wrong_text: Nora shakes her head. Give people the job they’ve already practised.

hints: Each skill is something Nora watched them do.
Wedge marks on the hatch. Turns recited with eyes shut. A pencil map of the water.
Match each mark Nora saw to a place on the route: a wedged hatch, a fork with no arrows, a gauge cabinet.
lines: i2_nora.jobs.01
i2_nora.jobs.02
i2_nora.jobs.03
jobs.finding: nora|Lyle keeps the hatch from catching. Dale remembers every turn. I take the pumps. Water is the one thing on this ship I understand.

pump.title: Gallery circulation
pump.goal: Lower the pressure at the hatch without starving the beds.
pump.background: Nora knows pumps from the aquarium. The Gallery runs on water too: one circuit feeds the beds, another returns it. Opening the hatch with the return pressure high would wake the whole hall.
lead: nora|Three service branches. Let’s see what each one does.
nora|The top dial reads an empty wash line. Ignore it. Watch the return and the bed flow.
nora|Bed flow has to stay at three or more. The return has to drop below three.
pump.prompt: Which branch should Nora open, and which dial should she trust?
pump.instruction: Pick the branch that keeps bed flow at 3 or more and drops RETURN below 3. Amber: upper 4, RETURN 7, bed flow 4. Blue: upper 1, RETURN 2, bed flow 4. White: upper 3, RETURN 2, bed flow 1.
hints: The upper dial reads an empty line. Watch the RETURN dial and the bed flow.
Amber keeps the beds fed but the RETURN is high. White drops the pressure but starves the beds.
Ignore the upper dial. You need bed flow of 3 or more and a RETURN below 3. Only one trial does both.
lines: i2_nora.pump.01
pump.finding: nora|The Blue branch keeps the beds at 4 and drops the RETURN to 2. The hatch can open, and nobody’s breathing changes.

message.title: Gallery intercom
message.goal: Leave a message for Steve, in case he ever comes.
message.background: The Gallery intercom has three message slots. If Steve comes at all, he might come on any watch. Only Steve should hear what Nora says.
lead: nora|If he comes. When he comes. He’ll come.
message.prompt: Where should Nora leave her message for Steve?
options: Slot A: plays in every bed now
Slot B: waits by this bed for PLAY
Slot C: clears when the watch changes

wrong.0: Every sleeper, and every guard, would hear it right now.
wrong.2: It would be gone by the next watch, and Steve could come on any watch.

hints: Who should hear it, and when?
It has to survive a change of watch, and only Steve should start it.
Rule out the slot every guard would hear and the slot that clears at the change of watch.
lines: i2_nora.message.01
message.finding: nora|My message for Steve is in Slot B, by my bed. It will wait for him.

recap: nora|I know every name in my row now. I have a route, a crew and a pump that behaves.
nora|The hardest part is the waiting. I have never waited quietly for anything. Between patrols I lie still and think about a man who went quiet for eighteen months.

outro.new: nora|Under the frost, something opened one enormous eye. It looked at me. Then it closed again.

lines: nora|How are you feeling, Dale?
dale|Cold, stiff and starving. If this is a hospital, the food is terrible.
nora|There isn’t any food here, Dale.
dale|That is exactly my point, Nora.
dale|Who is feeding June Calder’s beagle? I carry biscuits in my bag for her every morning.
nora|I’m sure somebody is looking after Biscuit.
dale|Somebody had better be. She sulks at anyone who forgets.
dale|Left at the pipes, right at the cold one, straight past the humming wall.
nora|You really did learn the whole route.
dale|Mail carriers never forget a route, Nora. We only forget birthdays.
lyle|My boys have a game on Saturday. I’ve missed most of their games this year.
nora|Then you’ll make the next one, Lyle.
lyle|Every single one, when I get out of here. I swear it.
lyle|I should be at work. Somebody must be covering my shifts.
nora|I think somebody probably is, Lyle.
lyle|Then I hope he’s nicer to Steve Mercer than I was.
